name: eNature
basis: Aleman, Wang & Schaeffel 2018, Sci Rep 8:10840; Swiatczak & Schaeffel 2022, TVST; Ingrassia et al. 2024, Vision Res; plus follow-up literature to 2025. Not medical advice.

research_grounding.citation: Aleman, A. C., Wang, M., & Schaeffel, F. (2018). Reading and Myopia: Contrast Polarity Matters. Scientific Reports, 8:10840. DOI:10.1038/s41598-018-28904-x
research_grounding.retinal_pathway: Stimulates the retinal ON-pathway through positive contrast polarity, promoting choroidal thickening (+10 µm) and inhibiting scleral axial elongation, while perifoveal receptive fields (6° to 12°) drive the 34.4 arcmin low-spatial-frequency requirement (~5 cycles/deg).
research_grounding.variants_summary: Two calibrated core versions: eNature Dark (default positive-contrast baseline 16.48:1, myopia-informed) and eNature Light (16.34:1 daylight fallback for proofreading and older eyes, explicitly documented as NOT myopia-informed).

protocol.status: Precautionary defaults, not a treatment and not guaranteed. Nothing here is proven to prevent myopia in people.

viewing_distance_cm.basis: Close reading under 30 cm and continuous reading over 30 min were risk factors in several studies; IMI guidelines cite under 20 cm and over 45 min.

session.break_activity: Look at a distant object with fine detail, ideally outdoors.
session.basis: Breaks every 30 min were protective in school studies. A 2023 trial found 20-second breaks did not ease eye-strain symptoms; a 2022 trial of 20-20-20 reminders in 29 adults did reduce them. Longer breaks are plausible but untested for myopia.

ambient_light.avoid: Reading a dark theme in a dark room
ambient_light.basis: 500 to 1000 lux thickened the choroid versus darkness in young adults. How this combines with dark themes is untested (inference).

protocol.outdoor_time: About 2 hours a day for children; the best-supported protective measure (IMI 2025).
protocol.small_screens: Phone-size text was the condition with no significant effect. Hold phones 40 cm or more, enlarge text, prefer larger screens for long reading.
protocol.under_3_years: No screens (WHO, AAP, Nov 2025 public health guidance).
protocol.pseudomyopia: If distance vision is blurry after near work and recovers over minutes to hours, or comes with headaches, see an eye doctor for a cycloplegic exam. A palette cannot treat accommodative spasm.

age_guidance.children_3_to_14: Outdoor time (about 2 h/day), distance of 40 cm or more (22px cap / 29px x-height) and regular breaks are the best-supported measures. Dark-mode benefit is unproven in children. eNature Dark with large text is an optional extra.
age_guidance.teens_and_young_adults_15_to_25: Highest-risk group for adult-onset progression (students, high myopes). eNature Dark, 40-60 cm (22px-32px), stop continuous near work at 30 min for 5-min distance break, outdoor time.
age_guidance.adults_25_to_40: Progression usually slows (<0.1 D/yr). Benefit of inverted contrast is uncertain; choose by comfort (eNature Dark or eNature Light); maintain 500-1000 lux room lighting.
age_guidance.adults_40_to_60: Presbyopia and uncorrected astigmatism dominate comfort; prioritize accurate near-work lenses; eNature Dark or eNature Light (27px-38px).
age_guidance.older_adults_60_plus: Clear lenses read better on eNature Light; lens scatter or cataract often favours eNature Dark (22px-32px+).

variant_roles.light: legibility fallback (16.34:1), daylight reading and older eyes, NOT myopia-informed
